briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 1, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Unprecedented Heatwaves and Health Emergency
sections.content: In July 2026, alongside the 'heat dome' phenomenon engulfing the world, record-breaking heatwaves exceeding 40 degrees Celsius are becoming commonplace both domestically and internationally [1, 6]. Notably, Yangsan, Gyeongnam, recorded an all-time high of 41.4 degrees Celsius, maintaining a severe heatwave warning for a week, and Central Asia's Kazakhstan is also suffering from extreme heat, indicating a global phenomenon [4, 21]. The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that these climate change-induced heatwaves are severely impacting health, with even summer camps struggling with heatwave and air pollution issues [26, 48]. Experts recommend walking in the early morning or evening during heatwaves, and predictions of temperatures potentially reaching 50 degrees Celsius have been raised, necessitating urgent action to protect human health [1, 20].

sections.title: ⚠️ Drought and Wildfires: A Catastrophe Burning the Earth
sections.content: Extreme climate change is leading to unprecedented droughts and wildfire disasters. Domestically, a shocking situation has been reported where riverbeds have been exposed due to severe drought, revealing even mammoth bones, suggesting that droughts are becoming more frequent and severe [8, 37]. Across Europe, large-scale wildfires have raged fiercely this summer alongside heatwaves and droughts, reaching 'unprecedented levels' [33, 39, 53, 56]. Specifically, in France and Spain, the likelihood of wildfires has increased by twofold and up to twentyfold, respectively, due to climate change, with Spain experiencing record-breaking fires in its hottest July on record [36, 40, 46, 49, 50]. In northwestern Ontario, Canada, over 150 wildfires broke out simultaneously, leading to the evacuation of thousands of residents, establishing wildfires as a serious climate disaster threatening our way of life [41, 58, 61].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts and Progress in Responding to the Climate Crisis
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, domestic and international efforts for climate change adaptation and mitigation are actively continuing. Incheon Michuhol-gu and Chungcheongnam-do are each accelerating the establishment of climate crisis adaptation plans and safety nets aimed at zero casualties, while the Ansan Environmental Foundation held an operational committee meeting for its Carbon Neutrality Support Center [2, 5, 7, 9]. In the business sector, NH Nonghyup Bank has issued Korean-style green bonds, and Hanmi Group and Hyundai E&C have announced strengthened investments in renewable energy and the promotion of RE100, contributing to the transition to carbon neutrality [10, 15, 16]. Furthermore, KEPCO is actively pursuing K-RE100 renewable energy projects utilizing idle substation sites, and Jeju is ushering in an era of building carbon neutrality through 'heating electrification' [11, 13]. Internationally, California has initiated public consultation on climate change reporting regulations, and the Zimbabwe Media Commission is validating a draft climate change reporting guideline, with each strengthening climate action in their respective capacities [23, 55].

sections.title: 🌍 Complex Impacts and Future Challenges of the Deepening Climate Crisis
sections.content: The climate crisis extends beyond mere weather anomalies, exerting complex impacts across society, economy, and ecosystems. The UN Secretary-General warned that El Niño is a 'prelude' to climate change, with the Earth entering 'uncharted territory' and 'burning,' which also poses risks to India's monsoon rainfall [30, 57]. Ecosystem disruption is becoming a reality, with changing migration patterns of great white sharks and a surge in shark sightings due to ocean overheating, and crop devastation threatening food security [44, 59]. Meanwhile, in the era of climate crisis, the dual nature of technology is also highlighted; alongside the positive aspect of AI being used to predict future oceans, AI data centers are mentioned as being behind the 'heat dome' phenomenon [3, 6]. Along with survey results indicating decreasing public interest in climate change, side effects of renewable energy transition, such as the issue of wind turbine waste, are also emerging as important future challenges [29, 51].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights that diverse response efforts are underway both domestically and internationally, even amidst an unprecedented climate crisis. A deeper understanding of the complex impacts of climate change and global cooperation are more critical than ever at this juncture. This concludes the climate briefing for August 1, 2026.
